newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end higher led by cement, banks.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end higher led by cement, banks.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended higher in trading that saw banks and cement companies among the day's biggest gainers.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose 0.52 percent to 16,771.19 on an above-average trading volume of 2.9 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB closed up 0.77 percent, meanwhile, ending at 1,068.76 on a volume of 1.2 billion.

Cement manufacturer Cementos del Caribe of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial group led winners with an impressive 3.58 percent move up in Medellin, where it closed at 5,697 pesos per share.

The highly diversified Sindicato Antioqueno is a darling of foreign investment funds and its Compania de Cementos Argos, also closed higher, ending up 1.59 percent in Medellin at 7,630 pesos per share.
"Argos is a solid share and demand for it dragged along Caribe," said one broker when asked about the gains.
He added that Caribe was attractive in and of itself, however, since "it weathered the 1996 recession in construction very well by increasing its exports."
Among banks, gainers were led by Banco Ganadero, which closed up 2.80 percent in Bogota at 330 pesos per share.
Brokers said local buying had apparently been fueled by demand for Ganadero's preferential ADRs in New York.

Banco de Colombia, Colombia's second-largest commercial bank after Ganadero, also closed higher as market players continued to jockey for position ahead of an expected move by Spain's Banco Central Hispanoamericano to buy up as much as 36 percent of the bank.
Extending the substantial gains it saw late last week, Banco de Colombia ended up 1.14 percent in Bogota at 441 pesos per share. ((-- Javier Mozzo, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944))
